All — attaching the DPA template (clean) and a lightweight subprocessor list for Novabank's review. Key notes: 
- Redwood uses SCCs + EU Addendum for EU customer exports to US where required. We maintain an internal attestation for subprocessors with SOC 2 or equivalent.

- We typically prefer DocuSign for enterprise envelopes; if a customer insists on AdobeSign we can accommodate but DocuSign is our default.

I've included suggested language for the data processing scope (see page 3 of the DPA). If Novabank has export control concerns for specific EU->US flows, we'll flag them to infra and propose contractual commitments.

Hannah — thanks for the patience. Rafael and Marissa attached our DPA and the requested matrix (see attachments). Quick answers to your numbered items below and a suggested next step.

1) DPA: Attached is our standard DPA (PDF). We're happy to receive redlines; for efficiency we can accept a redlineable Docx if you'd prefer but we'll start with the PDF on file.

2) Subprocessors & dataflow: See novabank-dataflow-matrix.xlsx. High-level: storage and logs live in EU clusters by default for EU customers; backup snapshots may be replicated to a US region for disaster recovery under SCCs. The file lists subprocessors and purpose.

3) Transfer mechanism: We use the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (2021) as a primary mechanism and a UK Addendum where applicable. For customers wanting additional safeguards (e.g., specific logging/segregation commitments) we can discuss in the DPA redline.

4) E-sign: Our preference is DocuSign (link below). If Novabank requires AdobeSign we can switch; tell us which contact should sign and we'll send an envelope.

Suggested next step: Rafael can send a DocuSign envelope with the DPA as the starting document; if Novabank submits redlines we'd expect them as a Docx or annotated PDF so our Legal Ops can review quickly.
